prompt: A raw-count token model assigns an unseen vocabulary word zero probability in spam, so one token wipes out the spam score. Which fix addresses this cause?

options.text: Take the logarithm of the zero probability.
options.explanation: The real logarithm of zero is undefined; logs do not fix zero estimates.
A product containing zero remains zero.

options.text: Use a larger floating-point type only.
options.explanation: The zero is a modelling estimate, not just numerical underflow.

options.text: Smooth counts within the fixed vocabulary.
options.explanation: Additive pseudo-counts give that token a positive class likelihood.

workedExample: Separate a genuine estimated zero from a positive number rounded towards zero. Smoothing fixes the first; log scoring helps prevent the second. Unknown tokens outside the fixed vocabulary still need a policy.
